h1: Rin Beach Resort — a Beachfront Resort in the Heart of Haad Rin You Can Walk to the Full Moon Party From
intro: If you're coming to Koh Phangan for the Full Moon Party, or you just want a beachfront base in the always-busy Haad Rin area, Rin Beach Resort is a spacious 3-star beachfront resort of around 78 rooms set on Haad Rin Nai — the quieter side that looks across to Koh Samui · What guests talk about most is the large swimming pool, the leafy grounds, and the overwater-style sea-view bungalows on stilts where you wake up with the water right in front of you · It's a short walk to Haad Rin Pier and across the headland to Haad Rin Nok, the Full Moon Party beach · Rooms start at roughly ฿1,000/night in normal season — but be clear that the scores are genuinely mixed: the location and setting stand out, while housekeeping and service swing a fair bit.

body.html: Rin Beach Resort sits on Haad Rin Nai, the quieter side of the Haad Rin headland that faces back toward Koh Samui — as opposed to Haad Rin Nok, the beach that hosts the Full Moon Party · The upside of this spot is that you get all the convenience of Haad Rin, but quieter nights than the party side · It's a few minutes' walk to Haad Rin Pier, where the ferries to Samui and Surat Thani dock, and a 5–10 minute walk across the narrow neck of land to Haad Rin Nok · For people who come to party but want a bed close by without driving in the early hours, this location works well.

What guests praise most is the generous space and the large swimming pool · Many reviews are surprised that a resort in Haad Rin has grounds this big — a large pool, plenty of sun loungers, leafy gardens and its own small private beach · The other highlight is the overwater-style sea-view bungalows on stilts, some of which reach out over the water with wide terraces for sitting and watching the sea — this group of rooms is what reviewers love most and photograph best.
"Opened the balcony door in the morning to a full sea view, sipped coffee watching the boats come and go, and the pool was big and uncrowded — a location like this in Haad Rin is hard to find."

But to be honest, the overall scores are genuinely borderline and the reviews split into two clear camps · The common complaint is inconsistent housekeeping and room condition — some guests find dated rooms with cracks, patchy cleaning, or the odd pest · There are technical niggles too: weak shower pressure, AC that doesn't cool in some rooms, Wi-Fi that drops, and rooms near the pool pump room that pick up machine noise · The picture is a resort with a good location and good space, but a building and upkeep that are starting to show their age — not every room is in the same shape.

Another recurring theme is front-desk service that swings — some guests meet friendly, helpful staff; others run into a cool reception or disputes over deposit deductions for minor stains · The private beach also needs managed expectations — it's small, the water is shallow in places and boats can block the view, so it's better for sitting and watching the sunset than for long swims · If you want a proper swim, use the resort pool instead.

The numbers reflect a resort that's strong on location and value, but not somewhere to expect polish — booking platforms sit around 7.6–8.0, while Tripadvisor is 3.0/5, ranked roughly #142 of 188 B&Bs/inns on Koh Phangan · Guests who arrive understanding this is a budget beachfront resort in a prime spot usually leave happy with the pool, the space and the views · Those expecting brand-new rooms or upscale-resort service can feel it doesn't match the photos.

Bottom line: Rin Beach Resort stands out for its beachfront location in Haad Rin, spacious grounds, big pool and sea-view rooms you wake up to the water in, at a price that's light for the area · It suits Full Moon Party-goers who want to stay close on the quieter side, people who love the Haad Rin vibe but want a calmer corner, and travellers who value the view and location over spotless rooms · But if you come to Koh Phangan for peace and quiet, brand-new spotless rooms, or upscale-resort service, this may not be it — look at Sri Thanu, Haad Yao or Thong Nai Pan instead.

A tip from reading the real reviews: if your budget allows, choose the sea-view rooms or the waterfront bungalows — that's what reviewers rave about, while the cheapest garden rooms are more hit-and-miss · Ask to see the room before taking the key if you can, and during a Full Moon, request a room on the Haad Rin Nai side to dodge the party noise at night · Book well ahead for full-moon nights, as Haad Rin fills fast and prices jump sharply.

honestSummary: Rin Beach Resort is a beachfront resort for travellers who want a central Haad Rin location, spacious grounds, a big pool and sea-view rooms at a budget price — ideal for Full Moon Party-goers who want to stay close on the quieter side · But you have to accept that housekeeping and service are inconsistent, the building is showing its age, and the reviews split clearly two ways.
honestChecks: If you expect brand-new rooms and upscale-resort polish — the building is dated and housekeeping swings → choose the sea-view rooms/waterfront bungalows, or consider a resort in Sri Thanu/Thong Nai Pan instead.
If you plan to swim properly off the resort beach — the private beach is small, shallow and partly blocked by boats → use the resort pool, or walk to Haad Rin Nok where the beach is longer.
If you're a light sleeper visiting on a full moon — party noise can carry across → request a room on the Haad Rin Nai side away from the party and bring earplugs.

faqTitle: FAQ — Rin Beach Resort Koh Phangan

faq.q: Where is Rin Beach Resort and how do you get there?
faq.a: Rin Beach Resort is at 94/2 Moo 6, Haad Rin Nai, Koh Phangan, on the side that faces Koh Samui · It's about a 5-minute walk from Haad Rin Pier and a 5–10 minute walk across the headland to Haad Rin Nok, the Full Moon Party beach · From Thong Sala (the main town) it's roughly a 30-minute drive.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what rooms are there?
faq.a: In normal season it starts at roughly ฿1,000/night for an Economy/Garden room · Superior is around ฿1,400, a Sea View Bungalow around ฿2,200, and a stilted House Boat over the water around ฿2,800 · Rates swing with the season and spike on full-moon nights, so compare a few platforms and book ahead.

faq.q: Who is Rin Beach Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for Full Moon Party-goers who want a beachfront base close by on the quieter side, and for travellers who value location, a big pool and sea views at a budget price · It's not for those expecting brand-new rooms, polish or upscale-resort service — that crowd should look at Sri Thanu, Haad Yao or Thong Nai Pan.

faq.q: Can you swim at the resort's private beach?
faq.a: There is a small private beach, but the water is fairly shallow and boats can block the view in places, so it's better for sitting and watching the sunset than for long swims · For a proper swim, use the resort's large pool or walk to Haad Rin Nok, where the beach is longer.

faq.q: Is it noisy during the Full Moon Party?
faq.a: It's on the Haad Rin Nai side, which is quieter than Haad Rin Nok where the party is held, but music can still carry on full-moon nights · Request a room further from the party and bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper · The upside is you can walk back to your room afterwards without driving late at night.

faq.q: Why are the review scores so split?
faq.a: Because Rin Beach Resort is strong on location, space and the pool, but inconsistent on room upkeep and service · Some guests get a good sea-view room and love it; others get a dated room, weak showers or a cool reception and leave disappointed · The trick is to choose the sea-view rooms/waterfront bungalows and ask to see the room before taking the key.
